name: Reflection Man
summary: An eau de parfum by Lucas Sieuzac. Amouage lists aromatic and floral notes over a woody base and states a 25% oil concentration.
verification_note: Release year not confirmed on checked official page.
media_rights: Official product image; private prototype reference only. No reuse license verified.
editorial_context: Amouage frames Reflection Man as a study in contrast: an aromatic, peppery opening of rosemary, red pepper berries and bitter orange leaves gives way to a powdery floral heart of neroli, orris and jasmine, before settling into a woody base of vetiver, patchouli, sandalwood and cedarwood. The house lists the eau de parfum at a 25% oil concentration, higher than many mainstream EDPs, which the brand ties to the composition's stated depth. Amouage has not published a release year on the checked page, so this record leaves that field unconfirmed rather than inferring one from resellers.

name: Portrait of a Lady
summary: Dominique Ropion’s eau de parfum is presented by the house as a floral chypre centered on rose. The official page lists raspberry, patchouli and incense among its notes.
verification_note: Official Description and Details contain different note pyramids. Shared core only displayed pending clarification. Release year not verified.
media_rights: Official product image; private prototype reference only. No reuse license verified.
editorial_context: Frédéric Malle presents Portrait of a Lady as Dominique Ropion's take on the floral chypre, built around an intense rose accord layered with raspberry, patchouli and incense. The house's own product page is not fully consistent: its Description and Details sections list different note structures, so this record shows only the notes that appear in both rather than treating either version as more authoritative. A release year is not stated on the checked page and is left unconfirmed here rather than sourced from resellers.

summary: Created by Jean-Claude Ellena in 2006. Hermès describes this eau de toilette through woody and mineral notes, highlighting grapefruit, cedar and flint.
verification_note: Official highlights are marketing notes, not a disclosed formula or complete ingredient pyramid.

editorial_context: Hermès attributes Terre d'Hermès, released in 2006, to perfumer Jean-Claude Ellena and describes it through a woody, mineral vocabulary: grapefruit for brightness, cedar for structure and a 'flint' accord meant to suggest stone struck against metal. These are the house's own highlighted notes rather than a disclosed ingredient pyramid, and Hermès does not publish a complete formula on its official product page.
